meta.description: Reference-anchored neighbourhood-overlap residual for network intrusion analysis and trust-based safety filtering
meta.note: This JSON summarises the experimental outcomes reported in the manuscript. Full per-seed tables are produced by the pipeline scripts under results/ when experiments are re-run.

summary.finding: Adding the residual did not raise clean F1 above features-only Random Forest. Residual-only conformal detector was weak (F1 ~0.01-0.29 public, ~0.08 Custom-EdgeIoT).

residual_suppression.note: Recall loss under adaptive search is comparable to random perturbation of the same size; residual is not a single point of failure.

summary.finding: Trust fell during both overt and authenticated attacks. Trust-adaptive filter reduced separation violations and collisions vs unfiltered controller; five seeds showed no clear advantage over fixed 3.0 m margin. Filtering raised goal-tracking error.

trust_adaptive.note: Required d_min = 1.5 m; global minimum still below requirement because compromised agents bypass the filter.

trust_dynamics.compromised_overt: drops to ~0.04 within one step, stays low
trust_dynamics.compromised_authenticated: drops to ~0.2, partial recovery around goal reversals

scaling.description: Wall-clock time of one complete filter step (all agents), sequential, test platform
scaling.note: Growth is approximately quadratic; 51 ms at N=30 is sequential CPU time on the evaluation platform.

limitations: No gain in clean F1 from residual on tabular detectors
No demonstrated advantage of trust-adaptive margin over fixed large margin (5 seeds)
Computation time grows with swarm size
Record-level random splits may be optimistic; chronological/host-disjoint splits not evaluated
Adversarial evaluation limited to 8 Gaussian perturbations; not protocol-preserving
Trust weights set by hand; no ablation of evidence terms
